Papilio crino.headline: Emerald swallowtail & emblem of The Nature and Butterfly Society
Papilio crino.upperwing: Velvety black dusted uniformly with sparkling emerald-green scales and crossed by a bright metallic blue-green median band across both wings.
Papilio crino.underwing: Dark brown dusted with pale ochre scales and a series of orange-ringed blue lunules along the hindwing margin.
Papilio crino.similarSpecies: Distinguished from Paris Peacock (Papilio paris) by the continuous median blue-green band across forewing and hindwing rather than a single isolated blue hindwing patch.
Papilio crino.habitat: Deciduous and dry evergreen forests, wooded foothill gardens, scrub jungles, and hill streams.
Papilio crino.behavior: Strong, rapid flier that hovers briefly while nectaring at Lantana and Clerodendrum flowers, and frequently mud-puddles along damp forest paths.
Papilio crino.season: Active throughout the year with peaks during and after monsoon months.
Papilio crino.tnDistribution: Widespread across Tamil Nadu hills and plains, including Kallar, Siruvani, Coimbatore, Pachamalai, and Salem foothills.
Papilio crino.wpaStatus: Protected in India under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
Papilio crino.notes: Recommended by TNBS members during state butterfly discussions (Pattampoochi Q2 2019) and depicted at the heart of the official TNBS society emblem.

Cirrochroa thais.headline: Tamil Nadu’s official State Butterfly (தமிழ் மறவன்)
Cirrochroa thais.upperwing: Warm bright orange crossed by fine dark wavy lines, dark forewing apex, and narrow black wing borders.
Cirrochroa thais.underwing: Paler ochre-orange with a prominent silvery-white median band (more pronounced in dry-season forms) bordered by dark brown lines.
Cirrochroa thais.similarSpecies: Looks superficially like the Cruiser (Vindula erota) male or Rustic (Cupha erymanthis), but lacks prominent yellow patches or hindwing tails and shows the crisp pale underside band.
Cirrochroa thais.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen hill forests, wooded streams, and shaded forest trails.
Cirrochroa thais.behavior: Strong, rapid flight along forest paths; puddles on damp sand and nectar-feeds in sunny clearings.
Cirrochroa thais.season: Recorded throughout the year, especially abundant post-monsoon across Western Ghats slopes.
Cirrochroa thais.tnDistribution: Western Ghats hill ranges of Tamil Nadu including Siruvani, Kallar, Mudumalai, Anamalai, Kalakkad-Mundanthurai, and Palani Hills.
Cirrochroa thais.notes: Officially declared the State Butterfly of Tamil Nadu in June 2019, Tamil Nadu became the fifth state in India to name a state butterfly.

Troides minos.headline: Largest butterfly of southern India and a Western Ghats endemic
Troides minos.upperwing: Vast velvety black forewings outlined with pale grey vein streaks paired with brilliant golden-yellow hindwings bordered in black scalloped patches.
Troides minos.underwing: Mirrors the dramatic black-and-gold upperwing pattern, with golden-yellow abdominal segments and scarlet-red hair tufts on the thorax.
Troides minos.similarSpecies: Unmistakable in Tamil Nadu by sheer wingspan and soaring canopy flight; females carry larger black triangular hindwing spots than males.
Troides minos.habitat: Evergreen and moist deciduous hill forests, foothills, coffee and cardamom estates, and forested valleys.
Troides minos.behavior: Soars effortlessly high in the forest canopy and descends early in the morning to feed on Mussaenda, Ixora, and Lantana blooms.
Troides minos.season: Seen year-round in wet hill forests, peaking between June and December.
Troides minos.tnDistribution: Western Ghats stretches of Tamil Nadu including Nilgiris, Mudumalai, Siruvani, Anamalai, Kodaikanal, and Kanyakumari.
Troides minos.notes: Also known as the Sahyadri Birdwing; Tamil Nadu’s largest butterfly species.

Pachliopta hector.headline: A bold red-bodied swallowtail common across plains and hills
Pachliopta hector.upperwing: Jet-black forewings crossed by two broken white bands and hindwings bearing two bright rows of crimson-red crescent spots; head and abdomen are bright crimson.
Pachliopta hector.underwing: Matches the crisp black, white-banded, and crimson-spotted dorsal pattern; red body acts as a warning signal of Aristolochia-derived toxins.
Pachliopta hector.similarSpecies: Separated from the Common Rose (Pachliopta aristolochiae) by the two distinct white bands across the black forewing and vivid crimson hindwing spots.
Pachliopta hector.habitat: Open scrublands, coastal plains, urban gardens, dry deciduous foothills, and cultivated landscapes.
Pachliopta hector.behavior: Flies slowly with effortless wingbeats just above vegetation and participates in local coastal and peninsular movements.
Pachliopta hector.season: Common throughout the year across Tamil Nadu.
Pachliopta hector.tnDistribution: Statewide from Chennai coast and interior plains to Western and Eastern Ghats foothills.
Pachliopta hector.wpaStatus: Protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (Schedule II).
Pachliopta hector.notes: Acts as the distasteful Batesian model mimicked by the female Common Mormon (hector form).

Pachliopta aristolochiae.headline: Red-bodied swallowtail with white-spotted hindwing centre
Pachliopta aristolochiae.upperwing: Black forewings with pale rayed veins and dark-tailed hindwings marked by a central cluster of white spots encircled by pinkish-red marginal lunules.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.underwing: Similar to upperwing; crimson thorax and abdomen clearly signal distastefulness to predators.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.similarSpecies: Lacks the bold white forewing stripes of Crimson Rose and displays a white discal patch on the hindwing; lacks the red body of Common Mormon mimics.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.habitat: Gardens, scrub, grasslands, agricultural edges, and forest clearings.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.behavior: Weak, unhurried flight close to nectar plants; rests with wings partly spread in morning sun.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.tnDistribution: Widespread across plains, wetlands, and hills up to mid-elevations.
Pachliopta aristolochiae.notes: Serves as the classic model mimicked by the 'stichius' form of the female Common Mormon (Papilio polytes).

Papilio polymnestor.headline: Tailless giant swallowtail with powdery pale blue hindwings
Papilio polymnestor.upperwing: Velvety black forewings streaked with pale blue post-discal bands and large pale sky-blue outer hindwings dotted with two rows of black spots.
Papilio polymnestor.underwing: Deep black with faint red basal patches and wide greyish-white outer hindwing area bearing black spots.
Papilio polymnestor.similarSpecies: Unmistakable in southern India, tailless, huge, and bright sky-blue on the outer half of the hindwing.
Papilio polymnestor.habitat: Wooded gardens, citrus orchards, moist deciduous foothills, and evergreen forests.
Papilio polymnestor.behavior: Glides powerfully through forest glades and feeds at Ixora, Mussaenda, and Lantana without settling still for long.
Papilio polymnestor.season: Year-round, with highest counts during monsoon and post-monsoon months.
Papilio polymnestor.tnDistribution: Common in the Western and Eastern Ghats (Mudumalai, Siruvani, Kallar, Pachamalai) and frequent in wooded plains and cities.
Papilio polymnestor.notes: TNBS checklist retains Papilio polymnestor for the Blue Mormon; Butterflies of India treats the taxon in the Papilio memnon/agenor complex.

Papilio polytes.headline: Classic garden swallowtail famous for female Batesian mimicry
Papilio polytes.upperwing: Males are black with a neat chain of white spots across the hindwing; females occur in three forms, male-like 'cyrus', Common Rose mimic 'stichius', and Crimson Rose mimic 'romulus'.
Papilio polytes.underwing: Dark brown-black with white discal spots and submarginal orange-red or white crescents depending on morph.
Papilio polytes.similarSpecies: Mimetic females have black bodies instead of the bright crimson body found in true Pachliopta rose swallowtails.
Papilio polytes.habitat: Home gardens, citrus groves, parks, scrub, and forest edges.
Papilio polytes.behavior: Active sun-lover weaving briskly through curry-leaf and lemon bushes while fluttering wings at flowers.
Papilio polytes.tnDistribution: Found in almost every district of Tamil Nadu from coastal cities to hill valleys.
Papilio polytes.notes: A textbook demonstration of polymorphic Batesian mimicry observable right in Tamil Nadu backyard curry-leaf plants.

Papilio demoleus.headline: Tailless black-and-yellow swallowtail common in citrus gardens
Papilio demoleus.upperwing: Black wings densely patterned with pale yellow spots and bands, accented by a blue-edged eyespot near the foremargin and a brick-red spot at the inner hindwing angle.
Papilio demoleus.underwing: Similar yellow-and-black mosaic overlaid with rich tawny-orange washes in the hindwing cells.
Papilio demoleus.similarSpecies: Tailless unlike most other yellow-and-black Papilio species, and lacks iridescent blue bands.
Papilio demoleus.habitat: Gardens, orchards, scrub, urban avenues, and open agricultural landscapes.
Papilio demoleus.behavior: Restless, fast-darting flight; settles briefly to mud-puddle on wet sand and bask with spread wings.
Papilio demoleus.season: Year-round, occasionally forming local migratory bursts (documented in Pattampoochi Q3 2018).
Papilio demoleus.tnDistribution: Ubiquitous across plains, foothills, and open hills throughout Tamil Nadu.
Papilio demoleus.notes: Young caterpillars mimic bird droppings before turning velvety green with eye-like thorax markings.

Papilio buddha.headline: Iridescent green-banded endemic swallowtail of the Western Ghats
Papilio buddha.upperwing: Velvety black outer wings with an exceptionally broad metallic blue-green basal and median sheen that shifts from emerald to turquoise in sunlight.
Papilio buddha.underwing: Dark brown dusted with fine scales and pale submarginal crescents on the hindwing.
Papilio buddha.similarSpecies: Differs from Common Banded Peacock by its much broader blue-green wing base and narrower black outer half on the forewing.
Papilio buddha.habitat: Dense evergreen and semi-evergreen hill forests, river valleys, and high canopy.
Papilio buddha.behavior: Canopy flyer that swoops down along forest streams and occasionally puddles on damp gravel in Mudumalai and Anamalai.
Papilio buddha.season: Mainly June to December, peaking during southwest and northeast monsoons.
Papilio buddha.tnDistribution: Western Ghats ranges of Tamil Nadu including Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, Anamalai, Nilgiris, and Tirunelveli hills.
Papilio buddha.wpaStatus: Protected in India under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
Papilio buddha.notes: Highlight sighting of the June 2024 TNBS Mudumalai Monsoon Butterfly Survey.

Papilio paris.headline: Black-and-green swallowtail carrying a glowing sapphire hindwing patch
Papilio paris.upperwing: Black thickly dusted with metallic green scales, illuminated by a large iridescent peacock-blue patch on the upper hindwing and a narrow green forewing line.
Papilio paris.underwing: Dull charcoal-black with a white-edged row of reddish-orange submarginal lunules along the hindwing.
Papilio paris.similarSpecies: Easily separated from Papilio crino by the brilliant square-ish blue hindwing patch instead of a continuous narrow band.
Papilio paris.habitat: Evergreen hill forests, moist forest clearings, streams, and shaded trails.
Papilio paris.behavior: Strong, patrolling flight; fond of sunlit stream-bed pebbles and wet sand.
Papilio paris.season: Recorded mostly during monsoon and winter across Western Ghats hills.
Papilio paris.tnDistribution: Nilgiris, Mudumalai, Siruvani, Valparai, Palani Hills, and southern Western Ghats.
Papilio paris.notes: Recorded during the June 2024 Mudumalai Tiger Reserve Monsoon Butterfly Survey.

Papilio liomedon.headline: Rare black-and-yellow swallowtail endemic to the Western Ghats
Papilio liomedon.upperwing: Dark chocolate-black crossed diagonally from forewing apex to inner hindwing by a continuous chain of bright creamy-yellow spots and long hindwing tails.
Papilio liomedon.underwing: Dark brown with matching pale yellow median band plus brick-red and blue submarginal rings on the hindwing.
Papilio liomedon.similarSpecies: Unique continuous straight yellow spot-band and pronounced spatulate tails distinguish it from all other Tamil Nadu swallowtails.
Papilio liomedon.habitat: Primary evergreen and moist deciduous hill forests of the Western Ghats.
Papilio liomedon.behavior: Strong canopy flier occasionally seen descending to hill-stream clearings and damp mud.
Papilio liomedon.season: Mostly July to November around monsoon showers.
Papilio liomedon.tnDistribution: Localized in Western Ghats pockets of Tamil Nadu (Anamalai, Nilgiris, Kalakkad-Mundanthurai; highlighted in Pattampoochi Q2 2022).
Papilio liomedon.wpaStatus: Protected in India under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.
Papilio liomedon.notes: A prized Western Ghats endemic documented by TNBS surveys.

Graphium agamemnon.headline: Fast-darting emerald-spotted swallowtail of gardens and hills
Graphium agamemnon.upperwing: Black wings spangled with dozens of bright apple-green rounded and bar-shaped spots; hindwing carries a short tail.
Graphium agamemnon.underwing: Warm purplish-brown mirroring the green spots, accented with tiny red marks along the hindwing base.
Graphium agamemnon.similarSpecies: Spot rows are broken into discrete emerald dots and short tails rather than the continuous pale turquoise band of Common Jay or Bluebottle.
Graphium agamemnon.habitat: Urban gardens, avenues with False Ashoka trees, foothills, and evergreen forests.
Graphium agamemnon.behavior: Restlessly vibrates its wings even while sipping nectar from Ixora and Lantana flowers.
Graphium agamemnon.season: Seen throughout the year across Tamil Nadu.
Graphium agamemnon.tnDistribution: Abundant statewide in both urban parks and hill forests.
Graphium agamemnon.notes: One of the easiest swallowtails to attract to urban gardens planted with custard apple or False Ashoka.

Graphium doson.headline: Tailless pale-cyan jay often mud-puddling along streams
Graphium doson.upperwing: Dark brown-black crossed by a central chain of semi-translucent pale aqua-blue spots and marginal spots.
Graphium doson.underwing: Silvery-brown with crisp crimson-edged black spots along the hindwing costal and discal region.
Graphium doson.similarSpecies: Separated from Southern Bluebottle (Graphium teredon) by the detached row of central spots and distinct red-centered dark spots on the hindwing underside.
Graphium doson.habitat: Forest streams, damp roads, foothills, parks, and woodlands.
Graphium doson.behavior: Rapid flyer that gathers in large mixed mud-puddling clusters along sunny stream beds.
Graphium doson.season: Common year-round, peaking in spring and post-monsoon.
Graphium doson.tnDistribution: Widespread across Tamil Nadu hills and wooded plains.

Graphium teredon.headline: Swift blue-banded swallowtail patrolling rivers and hill valleys
Graphium teredon.upperwing: Deep velvety black crossed diagonally from forewing apex to hindwing by a continuous, tapered turquoise-blue band.
Graphium teredon.underwing: Dusky brown repeating the turquoise band plus crimson spots near the hindwing margin.
Graphium teredon.similarSpecies: Formerly grouped under Graphium sarpedon; separated from Common Jay by its continuous central band and short tooth-like hindwing projection.
Graphium teredon.habitat: Forested hills, riverbanks, cinnamon-rich habitats, and shaded estates.
Graphium teredon.behavior: Glides rapidly along canopy gaps and congregates at damp sand patches in sunny forest clearings.
Graphium teredon.tnDistribution: Common across Western and Eastern Ghats including Kallar, Siruvani, Mudumalai, Kovai Kutralam, and Yercaud.

Eurema hecabe.headline: Abundant yellow pierid famous for mass movements in Mudumalai
Eurema hecabe.upperwing: Bright sulphur-yellow with deep black forewing borders sharply indented in the middle like the silhouette of an inverted '3'.
Eurema hecabe.underwing: Yellow speckled with variable brown smudges and exactly two small black spots inside the forewing cell.
Eurema hecabe.similarSpecies: Separated from Three-spot Grass Yellow (Eurema blanda) by having 2 (rather than 3) spots inside the underside forewing cell and a cleaner forewing tip.
Eurema hecabe.habitat: Grasslands, roadsides, gardens, agricultural fields, scrub, and forest edges.
Eurema hecabe.behavior: Weak fluttering flight close to the ground; gathers in bright yellow puddles on moist soil.
Eurema hecabe.season: Year-round statewide; thousands migrated together during the June 2024 Mudumalai survey.
Eurema hecabe.tnDistribution: Found across every habitat and elevation in Tamil Nadu.
Eurema hecabe.notes: During the June 2024 Mudumalai Tiger Reserve Monsoon Survey, TNBS recorded thousands of Common Grass Yellows moving together, a notable mass-movement event.
sources: New Indian Express, Mudumalai mass movement (2024)

Catopsilia pomona.headline: Strong-flying pale lemon-and-white emigrant with silver underside spots
Catopsilia pomona.upperwing: Creamy white with bright yellow wing bases (crocale/pomona forms) and black forewing outer margins.
Catopsilia pomona.underwing: Pearly greenish-white to pale yellow, plain or marked with silvery dark-ringed discal spots.
Catopsilia pomona.similarSpecies: Lacks the fine brown transverse wavy striations covering the underside of Mottled Emigrant (Catopsilia pyranthe).
Catopsilia pomona.habitat: Avenues, gardens, scrub, open plains, and hills.
Catopsilia pomona.behavior: Powerful, buoyant flight high over shrubs and trees; forms migratory streams alongside tigers and crows.
Catopsilia pomona.season: Common throughout the year; surges around pre-monsoon and northeast monsoon seasons.
Catopsilia pomona.tnDistribution: Statewide across plains, towns, and hill ranges.
Catopsilia pomona.notes: Participated alongside Danainae migrants during Tamil Nadu’s 2024 migration flights documented in Issue 27.

Delias eucharis.headline: Striking white butterfly with bright yellow and scarlet-spotted underside
Delias eucharis.upperwing: White wings crisply outlined with black veins and a black outer border framing white marginal spots.
Delias eucharis.underwing: Unmistakable bright saffron-yellow hindwing framed by bold brick-red heart-shaped spots inside a black border.
Delias eucharis.similarSpecies: Only Painted Sawtooth (Prioneris sita) approaches its red-and-yellow underside pattern, but Painted Sawtooth is restricted to wet hills and has red spots closer to the margin.
Delias eucharis.habitat: Avenues, gardens, orchards, dry and moist forests where mistletoe parasitizes host trees.
Delias eucharis.behavior: Flies slowly around tree canopies and glides gracefully down to Lantana and garden flowers.
Delias eucharis.season: Year-round, noticeably abundant in winter and dry months.
Delias eucharis.tnDistribution: Very common across Tamil Nadu plains, cities, and hills.
Delias eucharis.notes: Its bright red underside warns insectivorous birds of toxic compounds sequestered from mistletoe leaves.

Hebomoia glaucippe.headline: India’s largest pierid with blazing orange-tipped white forewings
Hebomoia glaucippe.upperwing: Chalky white with brilliant vermilion-orange apical patches edged in black at the forewing tips.
Hebomoia glaucippe.underwing: Mottled pale bark-brown underside camouflaging the butterfly cleanly against dry leaves when resting.
Hebomoia glaucippe.similarSpecies: Separated from smaller orange-tips (Ixias, Colotis) by its massive swallowtail-like wingspan and pointed forewing apex.
Hebomoia glaucippe.habitat: Forest streams, damp mud patches, deciduous hills, and shaded gardens.
Hebomoia glaucippe.behavior: Very fast, powerful flight above shrubs; congregates on wet sand alongside Graphium jays.
Hebomoia glaucippe.season: Seen throughout the year, peaking post-monsoon.
Hebomoia glaucippe.tnDistribution: Foothills and forests across Western and Eastern Ghats, including Kallar, Siruvani, Kovai Kutralam, and Pachamalai.

Leptosia nina.headline: Feather-light white butterfly drifting low over shaded weeds
Leptosia nina.upperwing: Translucent pure white marked by a single bold round black spot on the forewing and tiny dark apex.
Leptosia nina.underwing: White finely marbled with delicate pale olive-green striations across the hindwing.
Leptosia nina.similarSpecies: Rounded wingtips, fragile bobbing flight, and the solitary black forewing spot make Psyche unmistakable.
Leptosia nina.habitat: Shaded gardens, woodland edges, scrub undergrowth, and village hedges.
Leptosia nina.behavior: Weak, drifting bobbing flight just centimetres above shady undergrowth; rarely rises above waist height.
Leptosia nina.tnDistribution: Abundant across plains, urban green spaces, and hill foothills.

Belenois aurota.headline: Black-veined white pierid common in open scrub and plains
Belenois aurota.upperwing: Creamy white with broad black wingtips and margins punctured by clean white oval spots, plus a comma-shaped black forewing bar.
Belenois aurota.underwing: White veins starkly bordered in charcoal-black with yellow tinting on the hindwing and white marginal cells.
Belenois aurota.similarSpecies: Separated from Common Gull (Cepora nerissa) by the bold black hockey-stick cell bar on the forewing upper surface.
Belenois aurota.habitat: Dry scrublands, open plains, roadside weeds, and agricultural borders.
Belenois aurota.behavior: Brisk flight low over dry scrub; known for long-distance dry-season dispersal flights.
Belenois aurota.season: Most conspicuous during dry and post-monsoon months.
Belenois aurota.tnDistribution: Common in central, eastern, and foothill scrub regions of Tamil Nadu.

Colias nilagiriensis.headline: High-altitude clouded yellow endemic to Nilgiri and Palani shola-grasslands
Colias nilagiriensis.upperwing: Golden-yellow (pale greenish-white in some females) bordered by broad dark brown-black outer bands dotted with yellow spots.
Colias nilagiriensis.underwing: Ochre-yellow dusted greenish with a crisp silver-white centered pink-ringed hindwing spot.
Colias nilagiriensis.similarSpecies: The only Clouded Yellow occurring in Tamil Nadu, immediately separated from lowland grass yellows by its thick spotted borders and montane habitat.
Colias nilagiriensis.habitat: Montane grasslands, shola margins, and temperate hill gardens above 1,500 m.
Colias nilagiriensis.behavior: Flies briskly close to cold montane grassland turf, basking sideways with wings closed to absorb sun heat.
Colias nilagiriensis.season: Year-round in high hills, brightest between October and May.
Colias nilagiriensis.tnDistribution: Restricted to high-elevation Nilgiris (Ooty, Avalanche, Upper Bhavani) and Palani Hills (Kodaikanal).

Ixias marianne.headline: Dry-zone white pierid with bright orange forewing patches framed in black
Ixias marianne.upperwing: Chalky white with a broad vivid orange patch occupying the outer half of the forewing, enclosed inside a wide black margin.
Ixias marianne.underwing: Rich sulphur-yellow speckled with brownish spots and small white-centered eyespots.
Ixias marianne.similarSpecies: Distinguished from Yellow Orange-tip (Ixias pyrene) by its white ground colour above (instead of bright yellow).
Ixias marianne.habitat: Dry scrub, thorny jungles, open plains, and dry deciduous foothills.
Ixias marianne.behavior: Quick, low erratic flight through thorny caper bushes.
Ixias marianne.season: Year-round, particularly numerous in dry eastern and interior plains.
Ixias marianne.tnDistribution: Common across dry lowlands, Salem, Madurai, Tirunelveli, and Eastern Ghats foothills.

Appias albina.headline: Clean white forest pierid famous for hill-foothill seasonal flights
Appias albina.upperwing: Pure white in males with faintly dusted black forewing tips; females may be white or yellow with broader dark margins carrying white spots.
Appias albina.underwing: Unmarked satiny white or pale butter-yellow lacking prominent dark submarginal bands.
Appias albina.similarSpecies: More pointed forewings than Common Gull and lacks the bold dark underside border of Chocolate Albatross.
Appias albina.habitat: Semi-evergreen and deciduous hill forests, stream corridors, and dry-to-moist slopes.
Appias albina.behavior: Swifts along forest trails and forms dense white puddles on wet sandy stream banks.
Appias albina.season: Year-round in hills; abundant in Pachamalai Hills (Issue 27 survey).
Appias albina.tnDistribution: Recorded across Mudumalai, Siruvani, Kallar, and abundantly across Pachamalai Hills.

Tirumala limniace.headline: Key long-distance migrant across Western and Eastern Ghats corridors
Tirumala limniace.upperwing: Deep black wings patterned with translucent pale turquoise-blue streaks, rounded spots, and paired basal forewing stripes.
Tirumala limniace.underwing: Golden-brown underside mirroring the pale blue markings; males bear a small scent pouch on the hindwing.
Tirumala limniace.similarSpecies: Wider, paler blue streaks and rounded forewing spots distinguish it from the darker, narrower-streaked Dark Blue Tiger (Tirumala septentrionis).
Tirumala limniace.habitat: Scrublands, parks, hill forests, wetlands, and seasonal migratory flyways.
Tirumala limniace.behavior: Glides tirelessly along fixed directional flyways between the Eastern and Western Ghats during April–May and September–November.
Tirumala limniace.season: Year-round; huge directional aggregations recorded by TNBS in Sep–Nov and Apr–May.
Tirumala limniace.tnDistribution: Statewide; flagship species of TNBS’s 12+ years of Tamil Nadu migration monitoring.
Tirumala limniace.notes: Tracked annually by TNBS from Yercaud/Salem across Tiruppur and Coimbatore toward the Nilgiris and Anamalais (Issue 27 & Oct 2026 press).

Tirumala septentrionis.headline: Deep-blue forest tiger forming the backbone of September migrations
Tirumala septentrionis.upperwing: Velvety black wings etched with narrower, deeper sky-blue streaks and elongated spots.
Tirumala septentrionis.underwing: Dark chestnut-brown underside preserving crisp narrow pale-blue streaks.
Tirumala septentrionis.similarSpecies: Darker wing ground and much narrower, unbroken forewing basal blue streaks separate it from Blue Tiger (Tirumala limniace).
Tirumala septentrionis.habitat: Moist hill forests, wooded foothills, and seasonal migratory corridors across western plains.
Tirumala septentrionis.behavior: Gathers in dense overnight roosts in hill forests and surges across plains in steady migratory streams.
Tirumala septentrionis.season: Peaks dramatically from late September through November; documented at 10–200 butterflies/min over Coimbatore skies in Sep 2024.
Tirumala septentrionis.tnDistribution: Eastern Ghats (Yercaud, Pachamalai), Salem, Erode, Tiruppur, Coimbatore, and Western Ghats reserves.
Tirumala septentrionis.notes: Made up the majority of the 95% tiger share observed during TNBS’s September 2024 Coimbatore migration counts (Issue 27).

Danaus chrysippus.headline: Iconic orange-and-black monarch butterfly of open plains and gardens
Danaus chrysippus.upperwing: Warm tawny-orange with jet-black forewing tips slashed by a crisp row of white spots and a black-spotted hindwing centre.
Danaus chrysippus.underwing: Paler golden-orange with matching black borders and bright white spots.
Danaus chrysippus.similarSpecies: Unmarked tawny veins distinguish it from the boldly black-veined Striped Tiger (Danaus genutia) and the female Danaid Eggfly mimic (which lacks small black central hindwing spots).
Danaus chrysippus.habitat: Gardens, roadside milkweeds, dry plains, coastal dunes, and open hills.
Danaus chrysippus.behavior: Slow, buoyant flight; frequently visits Tridax, Lantana, and Calotropis blooms.
Danaus chrysippus.tnDistribution: Found in virtually all 38 districts of Tamil Nadu.
Danaus chrysippus.notes: Serves as the model mimicked by females of the Danaid Eggfly (Hypolimnas misippus).

Danaus genutia.headline: Black-veined orange tiger common across wetlands, plains, and hills
Danaus genutia.upperwing: Rich orange-tawny etched with thick black veins on every wing, black outer margins dotted with double rows of white spots, and white-barred black forewing apex.
Danaus genutia.underwing: Paler orange-brown repeating the bold black-veined pattern.
Danaus genutia.similarSpecies: Heavy black stripes tracing every wing vein cleanly separate it from Plain Tiger.
Danaus genutia.habitat: Wetlands, scrub, foothills, forest clearings, and gardens.
Danaus genutia.behavior: Unconcerned slow flight; gathers in small groups around Crotalaria plants to harvest pyrrolizidine alkaloids.
Danaus genutia.season: Year-round, peaking between September and February.
Danaus genutia.tnDistribution: Widespread across coastal, interior, and hill landscapes of Tamil Nadu.

Euploea core.headline: Velvety dark-brown crow butterfly common in cities and migration flights
Euploea core.upperwing: Rich glossy dark brown bordered by two neat submarginal and marginal rows of clean white spots across both wings.
Euploea core.underwing: Warm dark brown with clear white discal spots in addition to the twin marginal spot rows; males show a single short brand on the forewing.
Euploea core.similarSpecies: Separated from Double-branded Crow (Euploea sylvester) by having one (rather than two) parallel forewing scent brands in males and simpler white inner-forewing spotting.
Euploea core.habitat: Urban gardens, avenues, scrub, hill forests, and seasonal migratory flyways.
Euploea core.behavior: Slow gliding flight; males often visit dry Crotalaria or Heliotropium stems.
Euploea core.season: Abundant year-round; participates prominently in TNBS pre- and post-monsoon migration flights.
Euploea core.tnDistribution: Statewide across plains, towns, and hills.
Euploea core.notes: Mimicked by the Common Mime (Papilio clytia) and the female Great Eggfly (Hypolimnas bolina).

Euploea sylvester.headline: Deep-brown migratory crow with iridescent blue forewing sheen
Euploea sylvester.upperwing: Dark chocolate-brown bathed in deep violet-blue gloss on the forewing, bordered by white spots; males carry two prominent parallel velvety brands on the forewing.
Euploea sylvester.underwing: Dark brown with crisp white marginal and submarginal spot rows.
Euploea sylvester.similarSpecies: Two parallel forewing scent brands (in males) and rich blue sheen separate it from Common Crow.
Euploea sylvester.habitat: Moist foothills, hill forests, and cross-state migration corridors.
Euploea sylvester.behavior: Glides powerfully alongside Dark Blue and Blue Tigers during seasonal Western–Eastern Ghats migrations.
Euploea sylvester.season: Peaks during April–May and September–December migration waves.
Euploea sylvester.tnDistribution: Western & Eastern Ghats foothills, Mudumalai, Coimbatore, Salem, and Erode corridors.

Idea malabarica.headline: Giant translucent white-and-black glider endemic to Western Ghats wet forests
Idea malabarica.upperwing: Broad papery white wings veiled with charcoal-black veins and bold irregular black blotches and spots.
Idea malabarica.underwing: Identical translucent white-and-black pattern visible cleanly from below as it floats through the canopy.
Idea malabarica.similarSpecies: Unmistakable by size, papery slow flight, and translucent black-spotted white wings.
Idea malabarica.habitat: High-rainfall evergreen forests, shaded ravines, and undisturbed Western Ghats river valleys.
Idea malabarica.behavior: Floats gently like drifting tissue paper high among canopy lianas, occasionally descending to nectar at Ixora or Clerodendrum.
Idea malabarica.season: Seen throughout the year in wet evergreen pockets.
Idea malabarica.tnDistribution: Wet Western Ghats enclaves in Tamil Nadu: Nilgiris, Anamalai/Valparai, Silent Valley borders, and Kalakkad-Mundanthurai.

Parantica nilgiriensis.headline: Dusky highland tiger endemic to southern Western Ghats hills
Parantica nilgiriensis.upperwing: Smoky dark brown wings filled with narrow, muted bluish-grey streaks and tiny marginal dots.
Parantica nilgiriensis.underwing: Dull brownish-grey repeating the fine pale streaks, blending quietly in montane mist.
Parantica nilgiriensis.similarSpecies: Much darker, smokier brown ground colour and narrower dull streaks distinguish it from the pale lowland Glassy Tiger (Parantica aglea).
Parantica nilgiriensis.habitat: Shola forest margins, tea estates, and montane hill streams above 900 m.
Parantica nilgiriensis.behavior: Calm gliding flight around shola edges and Ageratina flowers in cool mountain sunshine.
Parantica nilgiriensis.season: Year-round in high Western Ghats hills.
Parantica nilgiriensis.tnDistribution: Nilgiris, Coonoor, Kotagiri, Valparai/Anamalai, Palani Hills (Kodaikanal), and Meghamalai.

Elymnias hypermnestra.headline: Pattampoochi Issue 27 checklist addition mimicking tigers on palm edges
Elymnias hypermnestra.upperwing: Mainland subspecies (E. h. undularis): males are velvety black-brown with pale blue marginal spots and reddish hindwing borders; females closely mimic Striped Tiger with black-veined orange wings.
Elymnias hypermnestra.underwing: Mottled bark-brown and cream cryptic striations camouflaging the butterfly against palm bark.
Elymnias hypermnestra.similarSpecies: Separated from Tailed Palmfly (Elymnias caudata) by rounded hindwings lacking a prominent tail projection.
Elymnias hypermnestra.habitat: Coconut groves, ornamental palm gardens, coastal parks, and humid hill orchards.
Elymnias hypermnestra.behavior: Shade-loving skulker around palm fronds; adults feed on tree sap and fermenting fruit juices.
Elymnias hypermnestra.tnDistribution: Added to the Tamil Nadu Checklist in 2024/Issue 27 following validated records around Chennai, Puducherry surroundings, and Sirumalai (Dindigul district).
Elymnias hypermnestra.notes: One of two latest species additions highlighted in Pattampoochi Issue 27 (Jan–Mar 2025, pp. 9–11), correcting historical assumptions that Andhra Pradesh marked its southern mainland limit.
sources: Pattampoochi Issue 27, A Note on Common Palmfly (pp. 9–11)

Melanitis leda.headline: Crepuscular brown butterfly masters of seasonal dry-leaf camouflage
Melanitis leda.upperwing: Dark earthy brown bearing a prominent black eyespot with two crisp white pupils and bright orange halos near the forewing tip.
Melanitis leda.underwing: Shows dramatic seasonal polyphenism: wet-season butterflies carry crisp concentric eyespots, while dry-season morphs turn into intricately mottled dead leaves.
Melanitis leda.similarSpecies: Common Evening Brown has larger orange halos around the white forewing spots than Dark Evening Brown (Melanitis phedima).
Melanitis leda.habitat: Shaded gardens, bamboo clumps, coconut groves, paddy bunds, and forest understorey.
Melanitis leda.behavior: Rests camouflaged among fallen leaf litter by day and becomes briskly active at dusk and dawn, feeding on ripe fruit and sap.
Melanitis leda.season: Year-round statewide; dry-season form dominates December–May.
Melanitis leda.tnDistribution: Very common across plains, farms, urban gardens, and forests throughout Tamil Nadu.

Acraea terpsicore.headline: Slender brick-orange butterfly of sunlit lawns and grasslands
Acraea terpsicore.upperwing: Narrow brick-orange wings dotted with neat black spots and bordered by a black hindwing margin spotted in white.
Acraea terpsicore.underwing: Paler orange-pink with glossy white marginal spots inside a black border on the hindwing.
Acraea terpsicore.similarSpecies: Elongated wings, black-and-white spotted hindwing margin, and long narrow abdomen distinguish it from leopards and fritillaries.
Acraea terpsicore.habitat: Sunny lawns, open fields, dry scrub, roadsides, and fallow gardens.
Acraea terpsicore.behavior: Weak, low leisurely flight; settles openly on grass blades and Tridax flowers.
Acraea terpsicore.tnDistribution: Common across Tamil Nadu plains, coasts, and open hills.

Cethosia mahratta.headline: Endemic serrated-wing beauty of Western Ghats wet forests
Cethosia mahratta.upperwing: Vivid fiery orange-red enclosed by heavily scalloped black borders and white subapical bands; females are duskier.
Cethosia mahratta.underwing: Spectacular mosaic of brick-red, white, black, and pale blue bands edged with delicate zigzags.
Cethosia mahratta.similarSpecies: Deeply scalloped wing edges and intricate multi-coloured lace-like underside make Tamil Lacewing unmistakable.
Cethosia mahratta.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, bamboo brakes, and hill streams.
Cethosia mahratta.behavior: Flutters gracefully through forest clearings and visits Mussaenda and Lantana blossoms.
Cethosia mahratta.season: Peak sightings from July to January.
Cethosia mahratta.tnDistribution: Western Ghats stretches of Tamil Nadu including Mudumalai, Siruvani, Anamalai, and Tirunelveli hills.
Cethosia mahratta.wpaStatus: Protected in India under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

Phalanta phalantha.headline: Bright orange leopard-spotted butterfly common in gardens and foothills
Phalanta phalantha.upperwing: Bright golden-orange thickly scattered with neat rows of rounded black spots and wavy marginal lines.
Phalanta phalantha.underwing: Glossy tawny-yellow washed with lilac sheen and delicate dark rings.
Phalanta phalantha.similarSpecies: More elongated forewings and crisp violet-tinted underside sheen separate it from Small Leopard (Phalanta alcippe) and Rustic.
Phalanta phalantha.habitat: Gardens, dry deciduous foothills, scrub, forest roads, and parks.
Phalanta phalantha.behavior: Brisk, darting flight; suns briefly on shrubs with flatly spread wings and sips flower nectar constantly.
Phalanta phalantha.tnDistribution: Widespread statewide from urban parks to hills.

Vindula erota.headline: Large tailed orange-and-olive brush-footed butterfly of hill streams
Vindula erota.upperwing: Males are bright golden-orange; females are dramatically larger, dark olive-brown crossed by a wide white median band.
Vindula erota.underwing: Ochre-orange in males or brownish-white in females with subtle violet wash and twin hindwing eyespots.
Vindula erota.similarSpecies: Short pointed hindwing tails and larger size cleanly separate Cruiser males from Tamil Yeoman.
Vindula erota.habitat: Moist deciduous and evergreen hill forests, especially along sunlit forest streams.
Vindula erota.behavior: Males puddle eagerly along damp forest tracks and stream pebbles; females patrol canopy clearings.
Vindula erota.season: Year-round in Western Ghats hills, peaking post-monsoon.
Vindula erota.tnDistribution: Mudumalai, Siruvani, Kallar, Anamalai, Palani Hills, and southern Western Ghats.

Moduza procris.headline: Rusty-orange woodland butterfly with a bold white cross-band
Moduza procris.upperwing: Rich brick-red and dark brown wings bisected across both wings by a striking clean white macular band.
Moduza procris.underwing: Pale greenish-grey base shading into warm rusty orange beyond the crisp white central band.
Moduza procris.similarSpecies: Bright brick-red upperwing ground combined with the bold white diagonal band makes Commander unmistakable.
Moduza procris.habitat: Forest stream banks, wooded foothills, damp trails, and riparian gardens.
Moduza procris.behavior: Glides smoothly over bushes, perches with wings spread flat on sunlit leaves, and paddles at damp sand.
Moduza procris.season: Common year-round in forested districts and foothills.
Moduza procris.tnDistribution: Western & Eastern Ghats foothills, Mudumalai, Pachamalai, Kovai Kutralam, and riverine green belts.

Neptis hylas.headline: Graceful black-and-white glider of scrub, gardens, and forest trails
Neptis hylas.upperwing: Velvety black boldly striped with clean white bands and a distinct white hockey-stick streak inside the forewing cell.
Neptis hylas.underwing: Warm golden-ochre underside with white bands sharply outlined in crisp fine black lines.
Neptis hylas.similarSpecies: Golden-ochre underside with crisp black outlines around the white bands distinguishes Common Sailer from Sullied and Short-banded Sailers.
Neptis hylas.habitat: Forest paths, village hedges, gardens, foothills, and open scrub.
Neptis hylas.behavior: Characteristic stiff-winged sailing glide alternated with quick shallow wingbeats.
Neptis hylas.tnDistribution: Found across every district in Tamil Nadu from coast to hills.

Parthenos sylvia.headline: Magnificent large emerald-and-pearl glider of Tamil Nadu hill forests
Parthenos sylvia.upperwing: Velvety olive-emerald wings crossed by translucent pearly-white forewing spots and bold dark tiger-like stripes.
Parthenos sylvia.underwing: Paler bluish-green echoing the translucent forewing window spots.
Parthenos sylvia.similarSpecies: Huge wingspan, translucent pearly forewing squares, and sweeping gliding flight make Clipper unique.
Parthenos sylvia.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, wooded waterfalls, and hill streams.
Parthenos sylvia.behavior: Powerful, soaring glider that perches high with wings spread flat and visits Mussaenda and Lantana.
Parthenos sylvia.tnDistribution: Western Ghats forests of Tamil Nadu including Kovai Kutralam, Siruvani, Mudumalai, Valparai, and Tirunelveli.

Euthalia aconthea.headline: Mango-feeding woodland butterfly with cryptic olive-brown upperwings
Euthalia aconthea.upperwing: Muted olive-brown wings etched with fine black cell loops and pale white spots (larger in females).
Euthalia aconthea.underwing: Warm ochre-brown matching dry mango bark and soil when settled.
Euthalia aconthea.similarSpecies: Separated from Baronet by dull olive-brown ground colour and from Redspot Duke by lacking bright crimson base spots.
Euthalia aconthea.habitat: Mango groves, home gardens, deciduous forests, and urban parks.
Euthalia aconthea.behavior: Fast buzzing flight close to the ground; basks with wings spread flat on sunlit paths and feeds eagerly on fallen mangoes.
Euthalia aconthea.season: Abundant year-round, especially during mango fruiting season.
Euthalia aconthea.tnDistribution: Common statewide wherever mango or cashew trees grow.

Vanessa cardui.headline: Cosmopolitan migrant recorded across hills and interior plains
Vanessa cardui.upperwing: Warm pinkish-orange wings patterned with black blotches and dark forewing tips dotted with bright white spots.
Vanessa cardui.underwing: Intricate marbled buff, rose-pink, and olive pattern bearing four neat submarginal eyespots on the hindwing.
Vanessa cardui.similarSpecies: Lacks the bright crimson-red forewing band of the Indian Red Admiral (Vanessa indica).
Vanessa cardui.habitat: Open grasslands, hills, dry scrub, fallow farmland, and urban gardens.
Vanessa cardui.behavior: Swift erratic flyer known for eruptive long-distance movements across Tamil Nadu.
Vanessa cardui.season: Irregular year-round; notable invasions documented in Pattampoochi (Q4 2019) and June 2026 Sivaganga press coverage.
Vanessa cardui.tnDistribution: Recorded from high Nilgiri/Palani peaks down to Sivaganga, Coimbatore, and coastal plains.
sources: Times of India, Painted Lady in Sivaganga (2026)

Junonia orithya.headline: Sun-loving grassland pansy with electric-blue male hindwings
Junonia orithya.upperwing: Males show velvety black forewings with cream bands and dazzling metallic sky-blue hindwings ringed by twin orange-edged eyespots; females are duller brown with larger eyespots.
Junonia orithya.underwing: Cryptic sandy-grey and brown dry-grass camouflage.
Junonia orithya.similarSpecies: Electric blue hindwing contrasting against dark forewings cleanly separates it from all other Tamil Nadu Junonia pansies.
Junonia orithya.habitat: Dry grasslands, open lawns, bare rocky paths, scrub, and hill meadows.
Junonia orithya.behavior: Perches flat on bare sunlit earth or short grass to defend small sunny territories.
Junonia orithya.season: Common year-round, especially in sunny dry weather.
Junonia orithya.tnDistribution: Widespread across plains, grasslands, and open hills in Tamil Nadu.

Junonia almana.headline: Rich orange wetland pansy with large concentric eyespots
Junonia almana.upperwing: Bright golden-orange marked with bold ringed eyespots, especially a huge multi-coloured peacock eyespot on each hindwing.
Junonia almana.underwing: Shows dramatic seasonal forms: wet-season butterflies carry crisp underside eyespots, while dry-season morphs have angular falcate wingtips and plain brown leaf-like undersides.
Junonia almana.similarSpecies: Bright orange ground colour and prominent giant peacock eyespots separate it cleanly from Lemon and Chocolate Pansies.
Junonia almana.habitat: Wetlands, marsh borders, paddy fields, garden lawns, and canal banks.
Junonia almana.behavior: Basks openly on low wetland plants and feeds eagerly on Tridax and Phyla blooms.
Junonia almana.tnDistribution: Abundant in wetlands and irrigated tracts across Tamil Nadu.

Junonia lemonias.headline: Olive-brown garden pansy spotted in pale lemon with bright eyespots
Junonia lemonias.upperwing: Olive-brown dotted with creamy lemon-yellow spots and bright blue-centered orange-ringed eyespots.
Junonia lemonias.underwing: Warm ochre-brown to dark reddish leaf-brown in dry-season forms.
Junonia lemonias.similarSpecies: Lemon-yellow forewing spots separate it from the uniformly dark Chocolate Pansy and grey-white Grey Pansy.
Junonia lemonias.habitat: Gardens, roadside weeds, agricultural edges, scrub, and forest trails.
Junonia lemonias.behavior: Low, brisk territorial flight; perches frequently on bare ground or low foliage with wings fully open.
Junonia lemonias.season: Very common all year across Tamil Nadu.
Junonia lemonias.tnDistribution: Occurs statewide from urban gardens to hills.

Junonia iphita.headline: Chocolate-brown pansy common along shaded trails and wet forests
Junonia iphita.upperwing: Rich dark chocolate-brown crossed by darker wavy bands and subtle pale marginal lines.
Junonia iphita.underwing: Resembles a veined dead leaf with a faint pale central line and small indistinct eyespots.
Junonia iphita.similarSpecies: Uniform deep chocolate-brown tones and lack of lemon spots or conspicuous large upperwing eyespots distinguish it from other pansies.
Junonia iphita.habitat: Wooded paths, shaded parks, hill forests, wetlands, and bamboo thickets.
Junonia iphita.behavior: Flies low along forest paths and sits flat on sunlit leaves in dappled shade.
Junonia iphita.season: Abundant year-round, especially in monsoon and winter.
Junonia iphita.tnDistribution: Common in both plains greenways and Western/Eastern Ghats forests.

Hypolimnas misippus.headline: Sexual-dimorphic eggfly whose female closely mimics Plain Tiger
Hypolimnas misippus.upperwing: Males are velvety jet-black with three brilliant violet-rimmed white ovals; females mimic the orange, black, and white Plain Tiger.
Hypolimnas misippus.underwing: Males show bold white bands on golden-brown; females show tawny-orange with a single large black spot at mid-hindwing costa.
Hypolimnas misippus.similarSpecies: Females lack the cluster of small black central dots inside the hindwing cell found in true Plain Tigers (Danaus chrysippus).
Hypolimnas misippus.habitat: Open scrub, lawns, gardens, roadsides, and fallow plains.
Hypolimnas misippus.behavior: Males defend sunlit perches and chase passing butterflies aggressively; females drift calmly like Plain Tigers.
Hypolimnas misippus.tnDistribution: Widespread across Tamil Nadu plains, coasts, and foothills.
Hypolimnas misippus.wpaStatus: Protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (Schedule II).

Hypolimnas bolina.headline: Large eggfly of wooded gardens and forests with iridescent egg spots
Hypolimnas bolina.upperwing: Males are velvety black with glowing violet-rimmed white oval spots on all wings; females vary from dark Common Crow mimics to orange-patched morphs.
Hypolimnas bolina.underwing: Dark brown crossed by a crisp pale scalloped submarginal chain.
Hypolimnas bolina.similarSpecies: Larger than Danaid Eggfly and bears white oval patches on all four wings in males (including small subapical forewing spots).
Hypolimnas bolina.habitat: Wooded parks, forest edges, gardens, and foothills.
Hypolimnas bolina.behavior: Males perch conspicuously high on sunlit shrubs and swoop after intruders.
Hypolimnas bolina.season: Year-round, peaking during monsoon and winter months.
Hypolimnas bolina.tnDistribution: Common across plains and hill forests throughout Tamil Nadu.

Kallima horsfieldi.headline: Famous Western Ghats leaf mimic flashing iridescent blue in flight
Kallima horsfieldi.upperwing: Deep indigo-blue crossed diagonally by a broad pale azure-white forewing band.
Kallima horsfieldi.underwing: Astonishingly realistic dry-leaf disguise complete with a central leaf midrib, fungal specks, and leaf-petiole hindwing tail.
Kallima horsfieldi.similarSpecies: Unmistakable: brilliant blue above, indistinguishable from a dead leaf when wings are snapped shut on tree bark.
Kallima horsfieldi.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen hill forests, stream banks, and shaded plantations.
Kallima horsfieldi.behavior: Darts swiftly between tree trunks and vanishes abruptly upon landing with folded wings to sip sap.
Kallima horsfieldi.tnDistribution: Western Ghats stretches of Tamil Nadu (Mudumalai, Anamalai, Nilgiris, Kalakkad-Mundanthurai).
Kallima horsfieldi.wpaStatus: Protected in India under the Wildlife (Protection) Act.

Charaxes bharata.headline: Fast-flying black-and-lime nawab adorned with twin hindwing tails
Charaxes bharata.upperwing: Velvety black wings bisected by a wide pale creamy-green median band and sporting two sharp hindwing tails.
Charaxes bharata.underwing: Pale satiny cream bordered by warm olive-brown margins and dark spots.
Charaxes bharata.similarSpecies: Previously known as Polyura athamas; separated from Anomalous Nawab (Charaxes agrarius) by subtly narrower median band and habitat overlap.
Charaxes bharata.habitat: Forest streams, damp gravel roads, foothills, and wooded clearings.
Charaxes bharata.behavior: Exceptionally fast flight; males puddle intently on wet sand, animal dung, and tree sap.
Charaxes bharata.season: Common year-round in hills and wooded districts.
Charaxes bharata.tnDistribution: Western and Eastern Ghats including Kallar, Siruvani, Mudumalai, Pachamalai, and Salem hills.
Charaxes bharata.notes: Featured on the back cover of Pattampoochi Issue 27 (photographed by Ramanasaran H).

Talicada nyseus.headline: Garden lycaenid prized for its black-and-white wings with orange rim
Talicada nyseus.upperwing: Velvety dark black-brown with a bright scarlet-orange patch along the lower half of the hindwing.
Talicada nyseus.underwing: Crisp snow-white checked with black spots on the outer forewing and a broad bright orange hindwing border.
Talicada nyseus.similarSpecies: Unmistakable in southern India, no other small lycaenid pairs a snow-white-and-black underside with a vivid orange hindwing border.
Talicada nyseus.habitat: Urban gardens, balconies, rocky outcrops, dry scrub, and wooded hillsides wherever Kalanchoe grows.
Talicada nyseus.behavior: Weak, low flight right around succulent host plants; caterpillars mine inside fleshy Kalanchoe leaves.
Talicada nyseus.tnDistribution: Abundant across cities, rocky hills, and gardens throughout Tamil Nadu.

Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.headline: Recently described Western Ghats silverline added in Issue 27
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.upperwing: Dark brown wings extensively marked with iridescent metallic blue across both forewing and hindwing.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.underwing: Buff-yellow crossed by metallic silver-centered dark bands: forewing discal and post-discal bands lie parallel from the costa, and the hindwing post-basal band is unbroken.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.similarSpecies: Diagnosed from all other Western Ghats Cigaritis (Spindasis) silverlines by the parallel conjoined forewing bands and continuous hindwing post-basal band ending at vein 1b.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.habitat: Montane cloud forest clearings and edges in the southern Western Ghats.
hostPlants: Myrmecophilous associations (documented with Crematogaster ants in original description)
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.behavior: Observed basking briefly on low vegetation along cloud-forest hill slopes.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.season: Documented around monsoon and post-monsoon months in high hills.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.tnDistribution: Meghamalai Hills (Theni district, Tamil Nadu), the type locality of this newly described species.
Cigaritis meghamalaiensis.notes: Described by S.R.K. Naicker, K. Sadasivan & colleagues in ENTOMON (2023) and formally added to the Tamil Nadu Butterfly Checklist in Pattampoochi Issue 27 (Jan–Mar 2025).
sources: Pattampoochi Issue 27, Cloud Forest Silverline Note (p. 11)

Castalius rosimon.headline: Dainty white-and-black spotted pierrot common in gardens and scrub
Castalius rosimon.upperwing: White wings with metallic pale-blue iridescent bases, dark margins, and bold scattered black spots.
Castalius rosimon.underwing: Pure white neatly spotted and streaked with jet-black marks and a delicate hair-like tail.
Castalius rosimon.similarSpecies: Differs from Angled Pierrot (Caleta decidia) and Banded Blue Pierrot (Discolampa ethion) by discrete scattered underside spots rather than solid dark diagonal bands.
Castalius rosimon.habitat: Scrublands, roadside Ziziphus shrubs, gardens, wetlands, and dry foothills.
Castalius rosimon.behavior: Weak fluttering flight close to thorny jujube bushes; mud-puddles at damp patches.
Castalius rosimon.tnDistribution: Common across plains, cities, and hills of Tamil Nadu.
Castalius rosimon.wpaStatus: Protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 (Schedule I/II history).

Lampides boeticus.headline: Long-distance migratory blue tailed with twin black eyespots
Lampides boeticus.upperwing: Males are soft frosted violet-blue; females are brown with blue wing bases; both carry two conspicuous black dots near the delicate hindwing tails.
Lampides boeticus.underwing: Pale buff-brown neatly rippled with white wavy stripes, a crisp white submarginal band on the hindwing, and twin orange-crowned black eyespots.
Lampides boeticus.similarSpecies: Rippled brown-and-white underside with a clean pale hindwing band separates it from Zebra Blue (which has stronger zebra-stripe contrast) and Ciliate Blues (which lack tails).
Lampides boeticus.habitat: Gardens, agricultural fields, fallow scrub, open hills, and Crotalaria patches.
Lampides boeticus.behavior: Brisk erratic flight around flowering legumes; famous global migrant.
Lampides boeticus.tnDistribution: Statewide from coastal plains to Nilgiri peaks.

Zizeeria karsandra.headline: Tiny grassland blue flying inches above urban lawns and pastures
Zizeeria karsandra.upperwing: Dull violet-blue broadly edged in brown (males) or plain brown with blue sheen (females).
Zizeeria karsandra.underwing: Pale grey-brown marked with neat rows of black spots and two small dark spots inside the hindwing cell.
Zizeeria karsandra.similarSpecies: Unlike Lesser Grass Blue (Zizina otis) and Tiny Grass Blue (Zizula hylax), it retains clear black dots inside the base of the forewing underside.
Zizeeria karsandra.habitat: Short lawns, parks, roadside herbs, playgrounds, and dry grasslands.
Zizeeria karsandra.behavior: Weak fluttering flight barely above grass blades; suns with half-open wings.
Zizeeria karsandra.tnDistribution: Found throughout all districts of Tamil Nadu.

Rachana jalindra.headline: Fast-flying mistletoe hairstreak highlighted in the Dec 2024 Pachamalai survey
Rachana jalindra.upperwing: Males are deep glossy violet-blue bordered in black; females are dark brown with bright white lower hindwing patches and twin delicate tails.
Rachana jalindra.underwing: Crisp pearly-white outer wing contrasting sharply against rich golden-brown inner wing halves separated by a clean straight dark line.
Rachana jalindra.similarSpecies: Two-toned golden-brown and snow-white underside with long white-tipped tails distinguishes Banded Royal cleanly from Broadtail Royal.
Rachana jalindra.habitat: Dense hill forests and forested slopes rich in parasitic mistletoe shrubs.
Rachana jalindra.behavior: Fast canopy flyer that settles briefly on high foliage and flower clusters.
Rachana jalindra.season: Peaks during post-monsoon and winter months.
Rachana jalindra.tnDistribution: Western Ghats (Kallar, Mudumalai, Siruvani) and a notable Eastern Ghats population recorded at Pachamalai Hills in December 2024.
Rachana jalindra.wpaStatus: Legally protected in India under Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Rachana jalindra.notes: Featured in Pattampoochi Issue 27 (Picture Stories & Pachamalai Hills Survey report, pp. 21–22), which recorded healthy numbers in thick Eastern Ghats forest.
sources: Pattampoochi Issue 27, Pachamalai Survey & Picture Story (pp. 21–22)

Rathinda amor.headline: Intricately patterned three-tailed hairstreak famous for twitching its false head
Rathinda amor.upperwing: Dull dark brown with an orange-white forewing spot and bright orange-brown lower hindwing bands.
Rathinda amor.underwing: Warm creamy-white intricately patterned with dark red-brown geometric blotches and carrying three delicate tails at the hindwing angle.
Rathinda amor.similarSpecies: Three filamentous tails paired with the geometric red-brown and cream underside make Monkey Puzzle unmistakable.
Rathinda amor.habitat: Scrub jungles, gardens, woodland trails, and coastal thickets.
Rathinda amor.behavior: Lands and instantly turns around while walking its hindwings up and down so its false head and tails fool predators.
Rathinda amor.tnDistribution: Common across coastal scrub, Chennai, Coimbatore, Pachamalai, and foothills.

Curetis thetis.headline: Coppery-orange and silver-white sunbeam of wooded edges and scrub
Curetis thetis.upperwing: Males flash brilliant fiery coppery-orange framed in black; females are dark brown with crisp white central patches.
Curetis thetis.underwing: Gleaming unmarked satiny silver-white on both sexes, making resting butterflies look like silvery leaves.
Curetis thetis.similarSpecies: Cleaner straighter underside post-discal dot row and slightly rounded forewing tip help separate it from Angled Sunbeam (Curetis acuta).
Curetis thetis.habitat: Forest streams, coastal scrub, wooded parks, and riverbanks.
Curetis thetis.behavior: Strong, rapid flight; basks with partially opened copper wings on sunlit foliage.
Curetis thetis.season: Year-round, common in winter and post-monsoon.
Curetis thetis.tnDistribution: Widespread across coastal, plains, and hill forests of Tamil Nadu.

Spalgis epius.headline: Unique carnivorous lycaenid whose caterpillars prey on plant mealybugs
Spalgis epius.upperwing: Dark smoky brown bearing a small pale white square patch near the middle of the forewing.
Spalgis epius.underwing: Silvery grey-white intricately scribbled with dozens of fine, wavy dark-brown lines.
Spalgis epius.similarSpecies: Fine scribbled grey-white underside lacks distinct black dots, bands, or tails, completely distinct from all grass blues.
Spalgis epius.habitat: Home gardens, orchards, coffee/guava farms, and forest edges hosting mealybug colonies.
hostPlants: Predatory caterpillar feeding on mealybugs (Planococcus / Ferrisia species) rather than plant foliage
Spalgis epius.behavior: Hovers briskly around mealybug-infested hibiscus, citrus, or guava shoots; its pupa remarkably resembles a tiny rhesus-monkey face.
Spalgis epius.tnDistribution: Found quietly across Tamil Nadu gardens, farms, and forests.

Abisara echerius.headline: Shaded woodland metalmark common across Western and Eastern Ghats
Abisara echerius.upperwing: Velvety maroon-brown wings crossed by pale greyish-white subapical bands and bearing dark twin spots near the hindwing margin.
Abisara echerius.underwing: Warm purplish-brown displaying crisp white diagonal median bands and black white-ringed submarginal eyespots.
Abisara echerius.similarSpecies: Closely resembles Plum Judy (Abisara bifasciata); Straight Plum Judy typically shows narrower, straighter median bands and habitat preference across peninsular hills.
Abisara echerius.habitat: Shaded forest trails, bamboo groves, overgrown estates, and stream sides.
Abisara echerius.behavior: Bobs jerkily through forest shade, settling with half-open wings on upper leaf surfaces and pivoting smoothly right after landing.
Abisara echerius.tnDistribution: Widespread in Tamil Nadu hill forests and foothills.

Abisara bifasciata.headline: Double-banded metalmark of dense moist forests in Tamil Nadu
Abisara bifasciata.upperwing: Rich dark plum-brown crossed by two broader pale whitish bands towards the forewing tip.
Abisara bifasciata.underwing: Deep purplish-brown with crisp contrasting median and post-discal white bands and twin black hindwing eyespots.
Abisara bifasciata.similarSpecies: Often treated alongside Abisara echerius; TNBS lists both species separately across Tamil Nadu forest surveys (including Mudumalai & Pachamalai).
Abisara bifasciata.habitat: Moist evergreen and deciduous hill forests and bamboo undergrowth.
Abisara bifasciata.behavior: Restless shaded flier turning abruptly after landing on leaves at eye level.
Abisara bifasciata.tnDistribution: Recorded in Western Ghats reserves (Mudumalai) and Eastern Ghats (Pachamalai).

Udaspes folus.headline: Bold black-and-white skipper of ginger and turmeric patches
Udaspes folus.upperwing: Jet-black wings boldly marked with semi-translucent pure white forewing spots and a single large irregular white patch covering the hindwing centre.
Udaspes folus.underwing: Dark brown dusted pale along outer margins, highlighting the huge white central hindwing patch.
Udaspes folus.similarSpecies: The huge pure-white central patch on the hindwing separates Grass Demon cleanly from Common Banded Demon (Notocrypta paralysos), which has plain dark hindwings.
Udaspes folus.habitat: Moist gardens, ginger/turmeric plots, forest clearings, and shaded stream edges.
Udaspes folus.behavior: Fast-darting flyer that hovers at Lantana, Clerodendrum, and Ixora flowers and suns with half-open wings.
Udaspes folus.season: Common during and after monsoon rains.
Udaspes folus.tnDistribution: Widespread across gardens, farms, and hill forests of Tamil Nadu.

Caprona ransonnetti.headline: Dry-zone spotted flat featured in Pattampoochi Issue 27 Picture Stories
Caprona ransonnetti.upperwing: Warm golden-brown wings dappled with translucent white forewing spots and pale scalloped outer margins.
Caprona ransonnetti.underwing: Chalky pale creamy-white speckled with small brown dots on the outer half, strongly contrasting with its brown upperside.
Caprona ransonnetti.similarSpecies: Bright chalky-white underside with crisp brown marginal spots separates Golden Angle from Spotted Angle (Caprona agama).
Caprona ransonnetti.habitat: Scrub forests, dry deciduous foothills, open sunny trails, and roadside Urena thickets.
Caprona ransonnetti.behavior: Rests flat with wings wide open on sunlit leaves or underneath leaf blades; caterpillars cut and fold neat leaf shelters.
Caprona ransonnetti.tnDistribution: Widespread across plains, scrub hills, and Western/Eastern Ghats foothills.
Caprona ransonnetti.notes: Featured in Pattampoochi Issue 27 Picture Stories (p. 23), documenting abundant pale yellow-green caterpillars feeding openly in bright daytime sunshine on Urena lobata.
sources: Pattampoochi Issue 27, Picture Story: Golden Angle (p. 23)

Badamia exclamationis.headline: Pointed-wing swift awl known for sudden mass arrivals
Badamia exclamationis.upperwing: Elongated, narrow-pointed chocolate-brown wings marked on the forewing with fine translucent white exclamation-mark spots.
Badamia exclamationis.underwing: Pale greyish-brown with a dark spot edged white near the hindwing inner corner.
Badamia exclamationis.similarSpecies: Extremely narrow pointed forewings and slender exclamation-like translucent streaks separate it immediately from Hasora awls.
Badamia exclamationis.habitat: Wooded foothills, parks, avenues, coastal forests, and dry hill trails.
Badamia exclamationis.behavior: Lightning-fast flight; rests under leaves in shade and is often active early morning and late afternoon.
Badamia exclamationis.season: Year-round with sudden seasonal population surges.
Badamia exclamationis.tnDistribution: Recorded across plains, foothills, and hill forests throughout Tamil Nadu.

Hasora chromus.headline: Fast twilight-loving awl with a crisp white hindwing underside band
Hasora chromus.upperwing: Plain dark glossy brown with an orange-brown sheen at wing bases; females show two pale yellow translucent forewing spots.
Hasora chromus.underwing: Deep purplish-brown crossed cleanly on the hindwing by a narrow pure-white straight band ending at a dark tornal patch.
Hasora chromus.similarSpecies: Narrow, clean straight white hindwing band (without metallic green tint) separates it from White Banded Awl (Hasora taminatus).
Hasora chromus.habitat: Avenues, wooded gardens, foothills, and forest clearings.
Hasora chromus.behavior: Most active at dawn, dusk, and in overcast weather; settles under leaves during bright midday sun.
Hasora chromus.tnDistribution: Widespread from Chennai and Coimbatore avenues to Mudumalai and Pachamalai.

Gangara thyrsis.headline: Huge twilight skipper with crimson eyes feeding on palm fronds
Gangara thyrsis.upperwing: Massive dark chocolate-brown skipper bearing large square semi-translucent golden-yellow spots on the forewing.
Gangara thyrsis.underwing: Brown dusted lightly with pale greyish-blue scales across the hindwing.
Gangara thyrsis.similarSpecies: Much larger than Rounded Palm-redeye (Erionota torus) and wears square golden forewing spots plus crimson-red eyes.
Gangara thyrsis.habitat: Palm groves, wooded urban gardens, coconut plantations, and damp foothills.
Gangara thyrsis.behavior: Crepuscular, hides under leaves during daylight and darts rapidly among palm flowers at dawn and dusk; caterpillars coat themselves in fluffy white wax filaments.
Gangara thyrsis.tnDistribution: Cities, coastal palm belts, Coimbatore, and moist hill foothills.

Borbo cinnara.headline: Common grassland swift spotted across paddy fields and lawns
Borbo cinnara.upperwing: Olive-brown wings bearing neat pale semi-translucent white spots in a curved forewing arc.
Borbo cinnara.underwing: Olive-greenish brown with three neat separated white discal spots across the hindwing.
Borbo cinnara.similarSpecies: Three well-separated white spots in spaces 2, 3, and 6 on the underside hindwing distinguish Rice Swift from Pelopidas branded swifts.
Borbo cinnara.habitat: Paddy fields, lawns, gardens, wetlands, and hill clearings.
Borbo cinnara.behavior: Fast low flight from grass flower to flower; basks in jet-plane posture.
Borbo cinnara.tnDistribution: Statewide across wetlands, plains, and hills.

Spialia galba.headline: Tiny checkered black-and-white skipper basking flat on sunlit ground
Spialia galba.upperwing: Charcoal-black checkered neatly with crisp white spots across both forewings and hindwings.
Spialia galba.underwing: Olive-grey crossed by clean broken white bands.
Spialia galba.similarSpecies: Smaller and evenly checkered with black-and-white bars across the margins compared to African Marbled Skipper (Gomalia elma).
Spialia galba.habitat: Sunny lawns, dry scrub, rocky paths, fallow fields, and open plains.
Spialia galba.behavior: Darts rapidly inches above sunlit ground and perches with wings wide open.
Spialia galba.tnDistribution: Common across Tamil Nadu plains and open foothills.

Tagiades litigiosa.headline: Bold black-and-snow-white flat resting openly with spread wings
Tagiades litigiosa.upperwing: Dark brown-black forewings specked with tiny white spots paired with hindwings whose lower half is snow-white with crisp black marginal dots.
Tagiades litigiosa.underwing: Almost pure snow-white across the hindwing.
Tagiades litigiosa.similarSpecies: Cleaner snow-white lower half of the hindwing upper surface with discrete black marginal dots separates it from Common Snow Flat (Tagiades japetus).
Tagiades litigiosa.habitat: Moist hill forests, wooded streams, and shaded foothills.
Tagiades litigiosa.behavior: Darts swiftly along shaded forest trails and settles flat underneath or atop broad leaves with wings spread.
Tagiades litigiosa.tnDistribution: Mudumalai, Siruvani, Kallar, Pachamalai, and Western/Eastern Ghats.

Suastus gremius.headline: Sturdy brown bob patterned with bold black spots on a grey underside
Suastus gremius.upperwing: Warm dark brown forewing carrying square pale-yellow spots.
Suastus gremius.underwing: Smooth pale purplish-grey speckled prominently with sharp black dots across the hindwing.
Suastus gremius.similarSpecies: Distinctive sharp jet-black spots dotted across a smooth pale grey hindwing underside make Indian Palm Bob straightforward to identify.
Suastus gremius.habitat: Coconut plantations, urban palm avenues, coastal parks, and scrub.
Suastus gremius.behavior: Quick darting flight around palm shoots; visits Lantana and Ixora flowers in gardens.
Suastus gremius.tnDistribution: Common statewide across coastal towns, plains, and foothills.

Neptis palnica.headline: Endemic Western Ghats sailer awaiting validated Tamil Nadu sightings
Neptis palnica.upperwing: Black with creamy-white bands; forewing cell streak is broken into basal streak and detached triangular spot.
Neptis palnica.underwing: Deep warm chestnut-brown marked with creamy white bands.
Neptis palnica.similarSpecies: Separated from Sullied Sailer by creamier underside bands and warm reddish-brown underside ground.
Neptis palnica.habitat: Mid- to high-elevation evergreen and shola forests in the Western Ghats.
Neptis palnica.behavior: Glides smoothly along sunlit shola clearings.
Neptis palnica.season: Recorded seasonally in Palani and high Western Ghats ranges.
Neptis palnica.tnDistribution: Listed among the 4 checklist species awaiting validated TNBS sighting confirmation in Issue 27 (Jan–Mar 2025).
Neptis palnica.notes: Pattampoochi Issue 27 calls on field naturalists to watch for validated photographic records of Palni Sailer in Tamil Nadu.

Arhopala bazaloides.headline: Dusted oakblue listed among TNBS’s 4 target species awaiting validation
Arhopala bazaloides.upperwing: Males are deep lustrous purplish-blue; females are dark brown with purple wing bases.
Arhopala bazaloides.underwing: Pale lilac-brown marked with darker brown outlined bands and dusted with pale frosted scales toward the forewing apex.
Arhopala bazaloides.similarSpecies: Frosty pale dusting near the forewing apex underside helps distinguish Tamil Oakblue from other brown-banded Arhopala oakblues.
Arhopala bazaloides.habitat: Moist evergreen and semi-evergreen foothill forests.
Arhopala bazaloides.behavior: Skulks in shaded understorey and settles with wings closed.
Arhopala bazaloides.tnDistribution: Listed in Pattampoochi Issue 27 among the 4 species awaiting validated Tamil Nadu sightings.

Hasora badra.headline: Large brown awl awaiting validated photographic record in Tamil Nadu
Hasora badra.upperwing: Plain dark brown in males; females bear large pale yellow hyaline spots in the forewing.
Hasora badra.underwing: Warm purplish-brown lacking the crisp white hindwing band of Common or White Banded Awl, showing instead a small dark-ringed white spot at the cell end and dark tornal lobe.
Hasora badra.similarSpecies: Lacks the continuous pale hindwing underside band seen in Hasora chromus and Hasora taminatus.
Hasora badra.habitat: Shaded evergreen forests and wooded hill ravines.
Hasora badra.behavior: Crepuscular flier sheltering beneath leaves during midday.
Hasora badra.tnDistribution: One of 4 checklist species awaiting validated TNBS sighting confirmation in Issue 27.

Arnetta mercara.headline: Endemic Western Ghats forest hopper awaiting validated TN confirmation
Arnetta mercara.upperwing: Dark brown bearing small pale translucent spots toward the outer forewing.
Arnetta mercara.underwing: Rich dark chocolate-brown dusted with golden-ochre scales toward the outer half of the hindwing and dotted with tiny pale specks.
Arnetta mercara.similarSpecies: Dark chocolate underside suffused golden-ochre distally separates it from Vindhyan Bob (Arnetta vindhiana).
Arnetta mercara.habitat: Undergrowth of moist evergreen forests in the Western Ghats.
Arnetta mercara.behavior: Low, brisk flier along shaded evergreen trails.
Arnetta mercara.tnDistribution: One of 4 checklist species awaiting validated TNBS sighting confirmation in Issue 27.
